chapters.name: Unit 1 Part Two New Words

words.tr: v. 调整；使适合；使适应；
words.ex: He adjusted the chair to sit comfortably.
words.ex_cn: 他调整了椅子以便坐得舒服。
words.en: To adjust something means to change it so that it is more effective or appropriate, or so that it fits better.

words.ex: He plays baseball every weekend.
words.ex_cn: 他每个周末打棒球。
words.en: a game played especially in North America by two teams of nine players, in which a player hits a ball with a bat and tries to run around four bases on a large field before the other team returns the ball

words.ex: The toys are in the basement.
words.ex_cn: 玩具在地下室里。
words.en: The basement of a building is a room or area that is partly or completely below ground level.

words.tr: n. 一回；一次；发作；拳击比赛
words.ex: He had a bout of coughing last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚咳了一阵子。
words.en: A bout of something is a short period of time during which it occurs a lot or is especially severe.

words.ex: The child clings to his mother's leg.
words.ex_cn: 孩子紧贴着妈妈的腿。
words.en: If you cling to someone or something, you hold onto them tightly.

words.ex: He complains about the loud noise every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都抱怨噪音太大。
words.en: To express dissatisfaction, pain, or resentment, usually because of a particular situation or someone's actions.

words.ex: He filed a complaint about the noisy neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 他投诉了吵闹的邻居。
words.en: A complaint is a statement in which you express your dissatisfaction with a particular situation.

words.ex: She coordinates the team's schedule.
words.ex_cn: 她协调团队的安排。
words.en: If you coordinate an activity, you organize the various people and things involved in it. If you coordinate the different parts of your body, you make them work together efficiently.

words.tr:
adj. 跛腿的；残废的
v. 使成瘸子；严重损坏（削弱）；“cripple”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The crippled boy walked with a cane.
words.ex_cn: 这个跛腿的男孩拄着拐杖走路。
words.en: If someone is crippled, they are severely injured or disabled, especially in a way that makes it difficult for them to walk or move.

words.ex: He went to school despite the rain.
words.ex_cn: 尽管下雨，他还是去上学了。
words.en: Without being affected by; in spite of.

words.ex: He felt envious when his friend got a new bike.
words.ex_cn: 当他的朋友得到一辆新自行车时，他感到嫉妒。
words.en: If you are envious of someone, you want something that they have.

words.ex: The pilot flew a fighter jet over the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 飞行员驾驶一架战斗机飞越了山脉。
words.en: A fighter is someone who fights in a battle or war, or someone who is determined to achieve something despite difficulties.

words.ex: He couldn't hide his frustration after losing the game.
words.ex_cn: 他输掉比赛后无法掩饰自己的沮丧。
words.en: The feeling of being upset or annoyed as a result of being unable to change or achieve something.

words.ex: The storm caused the train to halt.
words.ex_cn: 风暴使火车中断了。
words.en: Halting is used to describe something that is done in a hesitant or faltering manner, often because of uncertainty or lack of confidence.

words.ex: He held the handrail while walking down the stairs.
words.ex_cn: 他下楼梯时扶着扶手。
words.en: A handrail is a rail that you can hold onto for support, for example when you are going up or down stairs.

words.ex: He suffered an indignity at the hands of the guards.
words.ex_cn: 他受到了守卫的羞辱。
words.en: An indignity is a situation or event that causes you to feel ashamed or embarrassed because it involves something that is unfair or insulting.

words.tr:
n. 小孩；
v. 开玩笑；
words.ex: The kid is playing with a ball.
words.ex_cn: 小孩在玩球。
words.en: A kid is a child or young person. As a verb, to kid means to tease or deceive someone in a playful way.

words.ex: He is knowledgeable about history and science.
words.ex_cn: 他对历史和科学都很博学。
words.en: Someone who is knowledgeable has or shows a clear understanding of many different facts about the world or about a particular subject.

words.tr: adj. 较低的；下游的；“low”的比较级； v. 降低；
words.ex: He sat in the lower row of the theater.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在剧院的较低一排。
words.en: If you lower something, you move it slowly downwards. If you lower something, you make it less in amount, degree, value, or quality.

words.tr:
v. 惊异于；惊异；
n. 令人惊异的人（或事）；
words.ex: I marvel at how fast she runs.
words.ex_cn: 我惊异于她跑得有多快。
words.en: If you marvel at something, you express your great surprise, wonder, or admiration.

words.tr: adj. 值得纪念的；难忘的；
words.ex: That vacation was a memorable trip.
words.ex_cn: 那次旅行是一次值得纪念的旅程。
words.en: Something that is memorable is worth remembering or likely to be remembered, because it is special or very enjoyable.

words.ex: The weather today is nasty and rainy.
words.ex_cn: 今天的天气令人不愉快，又阴又雨。
words.en: If you describe something as nasty, you mean it is very unpleasant, unattractive, or unkind.

words.ex: He changed his pace to match the group.
words.ex_cn: 他调整了步伐以跟上队伍。
words.en: The speed at which someone or something moves, or with which something happens or changes.

words.ex: The clock strikes precisely at noon.
words.ex_cn: 钟恰好在正午敲响。
words.en: In a precise manner; exactly.

words.ex: He punched the wall in anger.
words.ex_cn: 他生气地打了墙一拳。
words.en: To punch means to hit someone or something hard with your fist, or to make a hole in something using a tool.

words.ex: He regained his strength after rest.
words.ex_cn: 他休息后恢复了体力。
words.en: If you regain something that you have lost, you get it back again.

words.ex: He showed reluctance to speak in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他表现出不愿意在全班面前讲话。
words.en: Reluctance is an unwillingness to do something.

words.ex: He was severely injured in the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故中严重受伤。
words.en: If something is done severely, it is done in a very great or intense degree.

words.ex: He shoved his way through the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他挤过人群。
words.en: To push someone or something in a rough or careless way.

words.tr:
n. 雪橇
v. 乘雪橇
words.ex: The children enjoyed riding on the sleigh.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们喜欢乘雪橇。
words.en: A sleigh is a vehicle which slides over snow, usually pulled by a horse.

words.tr:
n. 琐事；少量
v. 玩弄；轻视
words.ex: He threw away a trifle of money on candy.
words.ex_cn: 他花了一点钱买糖果。
words.en: A trifle is something that is considered to have little importance, value, or significance. It can also refer to a small amount of something. As a verb, to trifle means to treat someone or something without seriousness or respect.

words.ex: The train went through a long tunnel.
words.ex_cn: 火车通过了一条长长的隧道。
words.en: A tunnel is a long passage which has been made under or through the ground, usually through a hill or under a river, to allow people or vehicles to travel through it.

words.tr: adj. 未受协助的；独立的；
words.ex: He solved the puzzle unaided.
words.ex_cn: 他未受协助地解开了这个谜题。
words.en: Without help from anyone or anything.

words.tr: adj. 不需要的；多余的；无用的；
words.ex: The unwanted clothes were donated to charity.
words.ex_cn: 不需要的衣服被捐给了慈善机构。
words.en: If something is unwanted, it is not wanted or desired.

words.ex: He felt unworthy of the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他觉得自己不配得到这个奖。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is unworthy of something, you mean that they do not deserve it.

words.tr:
v. 力劝；
n. 强烈欲望；
words.ex: My teacher urged me to study harder.
words.ex_cn: 我的老师力劝我更加努力学习。
words.en: If you urge someone to do something, you try hard to persuade them to do it.

words.ex: She experienced the thrill of adventure vicariously through her friend's stories.
words.ex_cn: 她通过朋友的故事间接体验了冒险的刺激。
words.en: If you experience something vicariously, you experience it through other people rather than by doing it yourself.

chapters.name: Unit 1 Part Two Phrases and Expressions

words.tr: phrase. 大约；大概；是个…问题
words.ex: It is a matter of time before he arrives.
words.ex_cn: 他到达只是时间问题。
words.en: used to refer to a situation or subject that is being discussed or considered

words.ex: He engages in sports after school.
words.ex_cn: 他放学后参加体育运动。
words.en: To participate or become involved in an activity.

words.tr: phrase. 泄露（秘密）；透露；假装
words.ex: She didn't let on that she knew about the surprise party.
words.ex_cn: v. 她没有透露她知道惊喜派对的事。
words.en: To reveal or disclose information, often unintentionally or reluctantly.

words.ex: Now that it is sunny, we can go outside.
words.ex_cn: 既然天晴了，我们可以出去了。
words.en: Used to introduce a reason or explanation, often implying that the situation has changed.

words.tr: phrase. 休假中；在休假；请假
words.ex: He is on leave this week.
words.ex_cn: 他这周在休假。
words.en: If someone is on leave, they are not working at their job because they are on holiday or have permission to be away.

words.tr: phrase. 务必确保；负责使…发生（或完成）
words.ex: See to it that the door is locked.
words.ex_cn: 确保门锁好了。
words.en: To make sure that something is done or happens.

words.tr: phrase. 设定步调；带头引领节奏
words.ex: He runs fast to set the pace for the team.
words.ex_cn: 他跑得很快，为团队设定节奏。
words.en: To establish a speed or standard that others follow.

words.tr: phrase. 使…受制于…；使…服从于…；使…面临…（常用于被动语态，表示受某种条件、规则或影响的约束）
words.ex: They subject the material to high temperatures.
words.ex_cn: 他们将材料暴露在高温下。
words.en: To cause someone or something to experience or undergo something, often something unpleasant.

chapters.name: Unit 1 PASSAGE Ⅰ New Words

words.tr: n. 就寝时间；睡觉时间；
words.ex: His bedtime is 9 p.m. every night.
words.ex_cn: 他的就寝时间是每天晚上9点。
words.en: The time when someone usually goes to bed.

words.tr:
adj. 过去的
n. 过去的事
words.ex: He liked to talk about bygone days with his grandfather.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢和祖父谈论过去的时光。
words.en: Belonging to an earlier time.

words.ex: Wheat is a basic commodity in many countries.
words.ex_cn: 小麦在许多国家是一种基本商品。
words.en: A commodity is something that is bought and sold.

words.tr: adv. 秘密地; 亲密地，十分信任地
words.ex: He told me the secret confidentially.
words.ex_cn: 他悄悄地告诉我这个秘密。
words.en: If you tell someone something confidentially, you tell them in secret, trusting that they will not tell anyone else.

words.tr:
adj. 依靠的；依赖的；
n. 受赡养者；
words.ex: The child is dependent on his parents for food.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子依靠父母提供食物。
words.en: A dependent person or thing is one that needs the support of another person or thing in order to exist or be successful.

words.ex: His devotion to his family is obvious.
words.ex_cn: 他对家庭的献身显而易见。
words.en: Devotion is great love, affection, or admiration for someone or something.

words.tr: n. 泄水闸门；防洪闸门
words.ex: The floodgate opened and water rushed out.
words.ex_cn: 水闸打开了，水涌了出来。
words.en: A floodgate is a gate that can be opened or closed to admit or exclude water, especially one that controls the flow of water in a river or canal. It can also refer to something that controls the release or admission of a large quantity of something.

words.ex: The old man is frail and needs help to walk.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人瘦弱，需要帮助才能走路。
words.en: Someone who is frail is not very strong or healthy.

words.tr:
n. 凝视；注视；
v. 凝视；注视；
words.ex: His gaze fixed on the sunset.
words.ex_cn: 他的凝视固定在日落上。
words.en: If you gaze at someone or something, you look steadily at them for a long time, for example because you find them attractive or interesting, or because you are thinking about something else.

words.ex: He bought the car impulsively.
words.ex_cn: 他有推动力地买了那辆车。
words.en: If you describe someone as acting impulsively, you mean that they act suddenly without thinking carefully about what they are doing, often because they are being controlled by their emotions.

words.tr: adj. 不安全的；无保障的；缺乏自信的；无把握的
words.ex: He feels insecure when he is alone at night.
words.ex_cn: 当他晚上一个人时，他感到不安全。
words.en: If you are insecure, you lack confidence because you think that you are not good enough or are not loved.

words.tr: n. 一圈；（人坐着时）大腿部；
words.ex: He ran three laps around the track.
words.ex_cn: 他在跑道上跑了三圈。
words.en: The upper part of the legs of a seated person; a single turn or round in a race or other competition.

words.ex: The children play on the lawn after school.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们放学后在草坪上玩耍。
words.en: A lawn is an area of grass that is kept cut short and is usually part of someone's garden or yard, or part of a park.

words.ex: We waited in the lounge before our flight.
words.ex_cn: 我们在登机前等在休息室里。
words.en: A lounge is a room in a house or public building where people can sit and relax. As a verb, to lounge means to lie, sit, or stand in a relaxed or lazy way.

words.ex: He gave a rose to his lover on Valentine's Day.
words.ex_cn: 他在情人节给情人送了一朵玫瑰。
words.en: A lover is someone who is in a romantic or sexual relationship with another person, or someone who enjoys a particular thing or activity very much.

words.tr: n. 药物；药物治疗；药物处理；
words.ex: He took his medication every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上吃药。
words.en: Medication refers to a substance used for medical treatment, especially a medicine or drug.

words.ex: The bird sang a melodious song at dawn.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿在黎明时唱出旋律优美的歌。
words.en: If something such as a voice or a tune is melodious, it is pleasant to listen to because it has a musical quality.

words.ex: He has a monopoly on selling ice cream in this town.
words.ex_cn: 他在这座小镇上垄断了冰淇淋的销售。
words.en: If a company, person, or state has a monopoly on something such as an industry, they have complete control over it, so that it is impossible for others to become involved in it.

words.ex: The cat sat motionless by the window.
words.ex_cn: 猫静静地坐在窗边。
words.en: If someone or something is motionless, they are not moving at all.

words.ex: She wears a nightgown to bed.
words.ex_cn: 她穿睡衣睡觉。
words.en: A nightgown is a loose dress worn in bed by women or girls.

words.tr:
adv. 在夜里；突然；
adj. 整晚的；
words.ex: The baby slept overnight in the crib.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿整夜睡在小床上。
words.en: If something happens overnight, it happens during the night or for the period of one night. It can also mean happening very quickly or suddenly.

words.ex: She pampered her baby with warm baths and soft blankets.
words.ex_cn: 她用温水浴和柔软的毯子细心照顾她的婴儿。
words.en: To treat someone very kindly, often too kindly, by letting them have or do whatever they want.

words.ex: He took a pill for his headache.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了一粒药丸来缓解头痛。
words.en: A pill is a small solid mass of medicine that you swallow whole.

words.ex: He sits on the porch and drinks coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在门廊上喝咖啡。
words.en: A porch is a covered shelter projecting in front of the entrance of a building.

words.tr: v. （使）迷惑；“puzzle”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 困惑的；
words.ex: He was puzzled by the simple question.
words.ex_cn: 他被这个简单的问题弄糊涂了。
words.en: If you are puzzled, you are confused because you do not understand something.

words.ex: The train runs on the rail.
words.ex_cn: 火车在铁轨上行驶。
words.en: A rail is a horizontal bar, typically made of metal or wood, used as a support or barrier; or a track made of steel rails along which trains run.

words.tr: n. 认可；识别；认识；承认；
words.ex: His hard work got recognition from his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他的努力得到了老板的认可。
words.en: The action or process of recognizing or being recognized, in particular.

words.ex: We sit together and reminisce about old times.
words.ex_cn: 我们坐在一起回忆过去的时光。
words.en: If you reminisce about something from your past, you write or talk about it, often with pleasure.

words.ex: The child was restless during the long meeting.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在漫长的会议中坐立不安。
words.en: If you are restless, you are unable to stay still or to be calm and happy, because you are bored or worried.

words.ex: She makes a scrapbook with photos and tickets.
words.ex_cn: 她用照片和票券制作一本剪贴簿。
words.en: A scrapbook is a book with empty pages where you can stick pictures, newspaper articles, or other things you want to keep.

words.tr:
n. 转移；移位；转变；轮班；
v. 变换位置；转移；换（挡）；轮班；
words.ex: The shift of power to the new government was sudden.
words.ex_cn: 权力向新政府的转移是突然的。
words.en: If you shift something or if it shifts, it moves or changes its position slightly. If someone's opinion, attitude, or behaviour shifts, it changes slightly, especially in response to a particular situation or event.

words.tr:
n. 幻灯片；滑梯；
v. （使）滑动；下滑；
words.ex: He showed a slide of his vacation photos.
words.ex_cn: 他展示了一张他度假照片的幻灯片。
words.en: To move smoothly along a surface while maintaining continuous contact with it; to pass or move quietly or smoothly; a structure with a smooth sloping surface for children to slide down; a decline from a higher to a lower level or status.

words.ex: He left his slipper under the bed.
words.ex_cn: 他把拖鞋落在床下了。
words.en: A slipper is a kind of soft shoe that you wear at home.

words.ex: The staff at the hotel are very friendly.
words.ex_cn: 酒店的职员非常友好。
words.en: The people who work for a particular organization or company, or a group of officers assisting a commanding officer.

words.tr:
v. 闲逛；散步；漫步；
n. 闲逛；散步；漫步；
words.ex: They stroll in the park after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他们晚饭后在公园里闲逛。
words.en: If you stroll somewhere, you walk there in a slow, relaxed way.

words.ex: He had a sore throat after singing all night.
words.ex_cn: 他唱了一整晚后喉咙疼。
words.en: Your throat is the back part of your mouth, where it connects to your neck. It includes the passage that leads from your mouth to your stomach and lungs.

words.tr:
v. 把…塞进狭窄的空间；把…藏入
n. 褶皱；零食
words.ex: He tucked the letter into his pocket.
words.ex_cn: 他把信塞进了口袋里。
words.en: If you tuck something somewhere, you put it there so that it is safe, comfortable, or neat.

words.ex: The watchful mother kept her eyes on the child.
words.ex_cn: 这位警惕的母亲一直盯着孩子。
words.en: If someone is watchful, they are careful to look for any danger or trouble.

words.tr:
adv. 好；对；满意地；
int. （用于表示惊讶，疑虑，接受等）好；
n. 井；
adj. 健康的；
words.ex: She sings well.
words.ex_cn: 她唱得很好。
words.en: In a good or satisfactory manner; in a thorough manner; in a manner that is appropriate or suitable.

words.tr:
adj. 偏僻的；离群的；孤独的；内向的
v. 撤回；撤退；“withdraw”的过去分词
words.ex: The cabin is in a withdrawn area, far from the town.
words.ex_cn: 小木屋位于一个偏僻的地方，远离城镇。
words.en: If someone is withdrawn, they are very quiet, and do not want to talk to other people. If something is withdrawn, it is taken back or removed.

words.tr: adj. 有皱纹的；皱皱巴巴的； v. “wrinkle”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The old man had wrinkled hands.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人的手有皱纹。
words.en: Having wrinkles or creases; not smooth.

chapters.name: Unit 1 PASSAGE Ⅰ Phrases and Expressions

words.tr: phrase. 好像...似的； 仿佛...一样
words.ex: He talks as though he knows everything.
words.ex_cn: 他说话的样子好像什么都知道。
words.en: used to describe how someone or something seems to be, or how someone behaves, when this is not the real situation

words.tr: phrase. 好像...似的； 仿佛...一样
words.ex: He talks as if he knows everything.
words.ex_cn: 他说话的样子好像什么都知道。
words.en: used to describe how someone or something appears or behaves, suggesting that the appearance or behavior is not real or true

words.tr: phrase. 值班的；当值的；值勤的；在上班
words.ex: The nurse is on duty tonight.
words.ex_cn: 护士今晚在值班。
words.en: If someone is on duty, they are working at a particular time.

words.tr: phrase. /adv. 下班的；不值班的；下了班的
words.ex: He is off duty today.
words.ex_cn: 他今天休息。
words.en: If someone is off duty, they are not working.

words.tr: 短语动词. 值班；当班；在岗
words.ex: He is on duty at the hospital tonight.
words.ex_cn: 他今晚在医院值班。
words.en: To be officially working or responsible for a particular task or area at a particular time.

words.tr: 短语. 下班的；不在值班的
words.ex: He is off duty after his shift ends.
words.ex_cn: 他的班结束后就下班了。
words.en: To not be working or responsible for work duties at a particular time.

words.tr: phrase. 清嗓子，指为了准备说话或缓解喉咙不适而用力呼吸发出声音
words.ex: He clears his throat before speaking.
words.ex_cn: 他在说话前清了清嗓子。
words.en: To make a noise in the throat, often as a preliminary to speaking or to attract attention.

words.tr: phrase. 苏醒过来；变得活跃；显得逼真
words.ex: The painting seems to come to life in the moonlight.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画在月光下似乎活了过来。
words.en: To become active or lively; to start to function or operate.

words.tr: 短语动词. 恢复生气；苏醒；重新活跃起来
words.ex: After the rain, the garden seemed to come back to life.
words.ex_cn: v. 雨后，花园似乎恢复了生机。
words.en: To return to a living state or to regain vitality after appearing to be dead or lifeless.

words.ex: They can't deprive her of her right to speak.
words.ex_cn: 他们不能剥夺她说话的权利。
words.en: To take something away from someone or something, leaving them without it.

words.tr: phrase. 打开闸门；比喻引发大量（情感、事件、问题等）涌现
words.ex: The new policy may open the floodgates to more people moving to the city.
words.ex_cn: 这项新政策可能会引发更多人涌入城市。
words.en: To remove restrictions and allow something to happen or be done, often leading to a large number of events or actions.

words.tr: phrase. 把……塞进；把…… tucked in 表示将某物（如衣服、被子、餐巾等）塞入或折叠收拢到某处
words.ex: The mother tucks her child in every night before bed.
words.ex_cn: 妈妈每天晚上睡觉前都会帮孩子把被子掖好。
words.en: To push, fold, or turn (the edges or ends of something, especially a garment or bedclothes) so as to hide them or hold them in place.

words.tr: phrase. 突然出现；重新露面；调大
words.ex: He didn't turn up to the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他没有出席会议。
words.en: To arrive or appear somewhere, often unexpectedly; to increase the volume or intensity of something.

chapters.name: Unit 1 PASSAGE Ⅱ New Words

words.ex: He needs additional time to finish the homework.
words.ex_cn: 他需要额外的时间来完成作业。
words.en: If something is additional, it is extra and is added to what is already there.

words.tr:
adj. 爱慕的；敬慕的；崇拜的
v. 爱慕；敬慕；崇拜；“adore”的现在分词
words.ex: The children are adoring their teacher.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们正在热爱他们的老师。
words.en: If you are adoring, you show a lot of love and admiration for someone or something.

words.tr: n. 阿尔茨海默氏症；老年性痴呆
words.ex: She was diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease at the age of 65.
words.ex_cn: 她在65岁时被诊断出患有阿尔茨海默病。
words.en: A progressive disease that destroys memory and other important mental functions.

words.ex: He showed appreciation for her hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他对她的辛勤工作表示欣赏。
words.en: Recognition of the quality, value, significance, or magnitude of people and things.

words.tr: adj. 一定会；密切相关的；有义务的； v. “bind”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is bound to win the race.
words.ex_cn: 他一定会赢得比赛。
words.en: If one person, thing, or situation is bound to another, they are closely connected with each other, and it is difficult for them to be separated or to escape from each other. If you say that something is bound to happen, you mean that you are sure it will happen, because it is a natural consequence of something that is already known or exists.

words.tr: adj. 卓越的；极好的；明亮的；灿烂的；
words.ex: He gave a brilliant answer to the math question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这道数学题给出了卓越的回答。
words.en: A brilliant person, idea, or performance is extremely clever or skilful.

words.ex: He is capable of solving hard math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他能解决复杂的数学问题。
words.en: If a person or thing is capable of doing something, they have the ability or potential to do it.

words.ex: The puppy is cute.
words.ex_cn: 这只小狗很可爱。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as cute, you mean that they are attractive, often in a childlike or youthful way.

words.tr: n. 伤残；失去能力；无能力；
words.ex: He has a disability that makes walking difficult.
words.ex_cn: 他有伤残，导致行走困难。
words.en: A disability is a physical or mental condition that limits a person's movements, senses, or activities.

words.ex: The loud music was a diversion from his worries.
words.ex_cn: 那嘈杂的音乐分散了他对烦恼的注意力。
words.en: A diversion is an action or event that attracts your attention away from what you are doing or should be doing.

words.ex: She waited eagerly for the results.
words.ex_cn: 她渴望地等待着结果。
words.en: If you do something eagerly, you do it with enthusiasm and excitement because you really want to do it.

words.ex: He showed strong emotion when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个消息时，表现出了强烈的情绪。
words.en: An emotion is a feeling such as happiness, love, fear, anger, or hatred, which can be caused by the situation that you are in or the people you are with.

words.tr: v. 授权；命名；给...权利（或资格）
words.ex: This book entitles you to a free gift.
words.ex_cn: 这本书使你有资格获得一份免费礼物。
words.en: If you are entitled to something, you have the right to have it or do it.

words.tr:
v. 咆哮；低声吼叫；发出隆隆声
n. 咆哮；怒吼声；轰鸣声
words.ex: The dog growl at the stranger.
words.ex_cn: 狗向陌生人咆哮。
words.en: To make a deep, guttural sound of anger or hostility, often by an animal.

words.ex: Every human being deserves respect.
words.ex_cn: 每一个人都应得到尊重。
words.en: A human being is a man, woman, or child.

words.ex: He solved the math problem independently.
words.ex_cn: 他独立地解决了这道数学题。
words.en: In a way that is free from outside control; not depending on another's authority.

words.tr: n. 相互作用；相互影响；互动交流；
words.ex: The interaction between the two chemicals causes a reaction.
words.ex_cn: 这两种化学物质之间的相互作用引起反应。
words.en: An interaction is a situation where two or more people or things communicate with or react to each other.

words.tr:
n. 小睡；打盹；
v. 小睡；打盹；
words.ex: He took a short nap after lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他午饭后小睡了一会儿。
words.en: If you have a nap, you have a short sleep, usually during the day.

words.ex: The paper proves his ownership of the house.
words.ex_cn: 这份文件证明了他对这所房子的物主身份。
words.en: Ownership is the state or fact of owning something.

words.ex: The popularity of this song grew quickly on social media.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌在社交媒体上的流行迅速增长。
words.en: The state or condition of being liked, admired, or supported by many people.

words.tr:
n. 压力；压强；
v. 对…施加压力；
words.ex: He feels pressure from his parents to get good grades.
words.ex_cn: 他感受到来自父母要取得好成绩的压力。
words.en: Pressure is the force that you produce when you press hard on something, or the force that is produced by a particular amount of gas or liquid in a confined space.

words.tr:
v. （猫等满足地）发出呼噜声；（机器等）发出隆隆声；（人）轻柔地说话
n. （猫发出的）咕噜声；（机器等）颤动声
words.ex: The cat purrs when she is happy.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫在开心时会发出呼噜声。
words.en: When a cat purrs, it makes a low, continuous, vibrating sound that shows it is contented.

words.ex: Reading a book gives me relaxation.
words.ex_cn: 读书让我放松。
words.en: Relaxation is the state or process of becoming less tense, anxious, or stressed.

words.ex: He remarked that the weather was nice.
words.ex_cn: 他评论说天气很好。
words.en: If you remark that something is the case, you say that it is the case.

words.tr:
adj. 居住的；常驻的；
n. 常住居民；
words.ex: The resident population grew last year.
words.ex_cn: 居住人口去年增加了。
words.en: A resident is someone who lives in a particular place or a person who has their home in a place.

words.ex: He rubs his hands together to warm them.
words.ex_cn: 他搓手来暖和它们。
words.en: To move one's hand or a cloth repeatedly back and forth on the surface of something with firm pressure.

words.tr:
n. 抓痕；刮伤；
v. 抓搔；刮；
words.ex: The cat left a scratch on the door.
words.ex_cn: 猫在门上抓出了一道抓痕。
words.en: If you scratch something, you rub your fingernails or claws against it, often because it is itchy or irritating.

words.tr: n. 安全；保障；防护措施；
words.ex: The school improved security to protect students.
words.ex_cn: 学校加强了安全措施以保护学生。
words.en: Security refers to the state of being free from danger or threat, or measures taken to ensure safety.

words.tr: n. 中风；划水动作；一击；
words.ex: He had a stroke last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年中风了。
words.en: A stroke is a medical condition in which poor blood flow to the brain results in cell death. It can also refer to an act of hitting or striking someone or something, or a gentle movement of the hand over a surface.

words.ex: He gave me a suggestion to eat more vegetables.
words.ex_cn: 他给我提了一个多吃蔬菜的建议。
words.en: A suggestion is an idea or plan that someone puts forward for consideration.

words.ex: He is receiving therapy for his back pain.
words.ex_cn: 他正在接受治疗以缓解背痛。
words.en: Therapy is the treatment of someone with mental or physical illness without the use of drugs or operations.

words.tr: v. 触摸；接触；“touch”的现在分词；
words.ex: The child is touching the soft blanket.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在触摸柔软的毯子。
words.en: If something is touching, it causes feelings of sadness or sympathy.

words.tr: adj. 无条件的；无限制的；绝对的
words.ex: She gave him unconditional love.
words.ex_cn: 她给了他无条件的爱。
words.en: If you describe something as unconditional, you mean that it is not limited or affected by any conditions.

words.ex: The veterinarian helps sick animals.
words.ex_cn: 兽医帮助生病的动物。
words.en: A veterinarian is a person who is qualified to treat sick or injured animals.

words.ex: Eating fruits gives you vitamin C.
words.ex_cn: 吃水果可以给你维生素C。
words.en: A vitamin is one of a group of organic substances which are essential in small quantities to the nutrition of most animals and some plants, and which are present in natural foodstuffs or sometimes produced within the body.

words.tr:
v. 摇摆；摇动
n. 摇摆；爱说笑的人
words.ex: The dog wagged its tail happily.
words.ex_cn: 狗开心地摇着尾巴。
words.en: If a dog wags its tail, it moves its tail from side to side, often because it is happy or excited.

chapters.name: Unit 1 PASSAGE Ⅱ Phrases and Expressions

words.ex: He is capable of solving hard math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他能解决困难的数学问题。
words.en: To have the ability, power, or skill to do something.

words.ex: Many readers identify with the main character's struggles.
words.ex_cn: 许多读者对主角的挣扎感同身受。
words.en: If you identify with someone or something, you feel that you understand them or their feelings and ideas.

words.ex: I helped him, and he gave me a gift in return.
words.ex_cn: 我帮了他，他送了我一份礼物作为回报。
words.en: If you do something in return for what someone else has done for you, you do it because they did that thing for you.

chapters.name: Unit 2 Part Two New Words

words.ex: His acceptance of the offer made everyone happy.
words.ex_cn: 他接受了这份提议，让大家都很高兴。
words.en: The act of agreeing to receive or undertake something offered.

words.ex: I don't like coffee anymore.
words.ex_cn: 我不再喜欢咖啡了。
words.en: If something does not happen or is not true anymore, it has stopped happening or is no longer true.

words.ex: His argument was clear and logical.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点清晰而有逻辑。
words.en: An argument is a discussion or debate in which people express different opinions about something.

words.ex: He asked for assistance with his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他请求帮助做作业。
words.en: The act of helping or supporting someone or something.

words.ex: I assume it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我假定明天会下雨。
words.en: If you assume that something is true, you accept that it is true without proof.

words.ex: The teacher showed a chart of temperatures.
words.ex_cn: 老师展示了一张温度图表。
words.en: A chart is a graphical representation of data, in which the data is represented by symbols, such as bars in a bar chart, lines in a line chart, or slices in a pie chart.

words.ex: The conflict between the two countries lasted for years.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家之间的冲突持续了多年。
words.en: A conflict is a serious disagreement or argument, typically a protracted one.

words.ex: The word 'home' has a warm connotation.
words.ex_cn: ‘家’这个词有温暖的含义。
words.en: An idea or feeling that a word invokes in addition to its literal or primary meaning.

words.ex: He conveyed his thanks with a smile.
words.ex_cn: 他微笑着表达了谢意。
words.en: If you convey information or a message, you communicate it to someone, often in a way that is not direct.

words.ex: He gave an emotional speech about his mother.
words.ex_cn: 他发表了一篇关于他母亲的感人演讲。
words.en: Something that is emotional is connected with people's feelings. If someone is emotional, they show their feelings very openly, especially because they are upset.

words.ex: The teacher put emphasis on reading every day.
words.ex_cn: 老师强调每天都要阅读。
words.en: Special importance, value, or prominence given to something.

words.ex: He exaggerates his achievements to impress others.
words.ex_cn: 他夸张自己的成就来给别人留下印象。
words.en: If you exaggerate, you indicate that something is, for example, worse or more important than it really is.

words.tr: adj. 根据事实的；真实的；
words.ex: His report is factual and accurate.
words.ex_cn: 他的报告是基于事实且准确的。
words.en: If something is factual, it is based on facts or concerns facts.

words.ex: He made a generalization from the data.
words.ex_cn: 他从数据中做出了一个概括。
words.en: A generalization is a statement that seems to be true in most situations or for most people, but that may not be completely true in all cases.

words.ex: He ignored the warning sign.
words.ex_cn: 他忽视了警告标志。
words.en: If you ignore someone or something, you pay no attention to them.

words.ex: He bought a raincoat, and it rained ironically the next day.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一件雨衣，讽刺的是，第二天就下雨了。
words.en: In a way that is contrary to what is expected and is therefore amusing or strange.

words.ex: He took his words in a literal sense.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的话按字面意思理解。
words.en: If you describe something as the literal truth or a literal fact, you are emphasizing that it is true.

words.ex: He is literally the best player on the team.
words.ex_cn: 他确实是队里最好的球员。
words.en: In a literal manner or sense; exactly.

words.ex: Calling time a thief is a metaphor.
words.ex_cn: 把时间称为小偷是一种隐喻。
words.en: A metaphor is a figure of speech in which a word or phrase is applied to an object or action to which it is not literally applicable.

words.ex: He misinterprets her words as anger.
words.ex_cn: 他误解了她的话，以为是生气。
words.en: To interpret wrongly; misunderstand.

words.ex: He misleads his friends with false stories.
words.ex_cn: 他用虚假的故事误导他的朋友。
words.en: If you say that someone has misled you, you mean that they have made you believe something which is not true, either by telling you a lie or by giving you a wrong idea or impression.

words.ex: He mistakenly took my book.
words.ex_cn: 他误拿了我的书。
words.en: If you do something mistakenly, you do it in a way that is wrong or based on a wrong belief.

words.ex: He learned a new phrase in Spanish.
words.ex_cn: 他学了一个新的西班牙语短语。
words.en: A phrase is a short group of words that people often use as a way of saying something. The meaning of a phrase is often not obvious from the meaning of the individual words in it.

words.ex: He decided to quit smoking last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年决定戒烟。
words.en: If you quit, or quit something, you stop doing it or leave it.

words.ex: He reacts quickly when he hears a loud noise.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到大声响时，他会迅速做出反应。
words.en: When you react to something that has happened to you, you behave in a particular way because of it.

words.tr: v. 重新思考；重新考虑；
words.ex: We need to rethink our plan.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要重新思考我们的计划。
words.en: To consider again, especially with a view to changing or altering.

words.ex: He gave her a romantic gift on Valentine's Day.
words.ex_cn: 他在情人节送了她一份浪漫的礼物。
words.en: If you describe something as romantic, you mean that it is connected with love or with a feeling of excitement and mystery associated with love.

words.tr:
adj. 最佳的；最高级的；过度的
n. 最高级；最高程度
words.ex: This is the superlative movie I have ever seen.
words.ex_cn: 这是我见过的最棒的电影。
words.en: The superlative form of an adjective or adverb is the form that indicates that something has more of a quality than anything else in a particular group.

words.ex: The translator helped him understand the French book.
words.ex_cn: 这位翻译员帮他理解了这本法语书。
words.en: A translator is a person whose job is translating writing or speech from one language to another.

words.ex: The instructions are unclear.
words.ex_cn: 这些说明不清楚。
words.en: If something is unclear, it is not obvious or easy to see, understand, or be certain about.

words.ex: He gave an unloving look to his child.
words.ex_cn: 他给了孩子一个冷漠的眼神。
words.en: If you describe someone as unloving, you mean that they do not show love or affection for other people.

words.ex: His parents were unsupportive when he wanted to be an artist.
words.ex_cn: 当他想当艺术家时，他的父母并不支持。
words.en: If you describe someone as unsupportive, you mean that they do not give you help or encouragement.

words.ex: He spoke unsupportively when she shared her news.
words.ex_cn: 当她分享她的消息时，他以不支持的方式说话。
words.en: In a manner that does not provide support or approval.

words.ex: The car stopped at the verge of the road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车停在了道路的边缘。
words.en: The edge or border of something; to be close to a certain state or condition.

chapters.name: Unit 2 Part Two Phrases and Expressions

words.ex: I feel like eating pizza tonight.
words.ex_cn: 我今晚想吃披萨。
words.en: To have a desire or inclination for something; to have a sensation or impression of being a certain way.

words.tr: 为了产生某种效果；为了给人印象
words.ex: He spoke slowly for effect.
words.ex_cn: 他说话很慢，为了产生效果。
words.en: In order to create a particular impression or to be deliberately dramatic.

words.ex: The path will lead to the park.
words.ex_cn: 这条路会把人带到公园。
words.en: If an action or event leads to a particular situation or event, it causes that situation or event to happen.

words.tr: phrase. 接近于；濒临于；在···边缘
words.ex: He is on the verge of crying.
words.ex_cn: 他快要哭了。
words.en: If you are on the verge of something, you are very close to experiencing it.

words.tr: phrase. 拔出；驶离路边；退出
words.ex: He pulled out a coin from his pocket.
words.ex_cn: 他从口袋里掏出了一枚硬币。
words.en: To remove something or someone from a place or situation.

words.tr: phrase. phr. 轻视…；不当回事；不认真对待…
words.ex: He does not take his job lightly.
words.ex_cn: 他不轻视自己的工作。
words.en: To not consider something as serious or important as it should be.

chapters.name: Unit 2 PASSAGE Ⅰ New Words

words.ex: Graduating with honors was her greatest accomplishment.
words.ex_cn: 以优异成绩毕业是她最大的成就。
words.en: Something that has been achieved successfully.

words.ex: Her courage in facing danger is admirable.
words.ex_cn: 她在面对危险时表现出的勇气令人钦佩。
words.en: If you say that something is admirable, you mean that you approve of it or respect it.

words.ex: He felt admiration for his teacher's patience.
words.ex_cn: 他对他老师的耐心感到钦佩。
words.en: Admiration is a feeling of great liking and respect for someone or something.

words.ex: The old house has a mysterious aura.
words.ex_cn: 这所老房子有一种神秘的氛围。
words.en: An aura is a distinctive atmosphere or quality that seems to surround and be generated by a person, thing, or place.

words.ex: The sun shone brightly through the window.
words.ex_cn: 阳光明亮地照进窗户。
words.en: In a manner that is full of light or shining strongly; in a way that is cheerful and lively.

words.tr: adv. 高高兴兴地；愉快地
words.ex: She sang cheerfully while walking to school.
words.ex_cn: 她一边走路去学校，一边愉快地唱歌。
words.en: In a way that shows happiness or optimism.

words.ex: The chick is following its mother.
words.ex_cn: 小鸡跟着它的妈妈。
words.en: A chick is a baby bird, especially a baby chicken.

words.ex: He cannot comprehend the simple math problem.
words.ex_cn: 他无法理解这个简单的数学问题。
words.en: To comprehend something means to understand it fully.

words.ex: His determination helped him finish the race.
words.ex_cn: 他的决心帮助他完成了比赛。
words.en: Determination is the quality that you show when you have decided to do something and you will not let anything stop you.

words.ex: The two colors distinguish the two teams.
words.ex_cn: 这两种颜色使两个队伍有所不同。
words.en: If you can distinguish one thing from another, you can see or understand how they are different.

words.tr:
v. 害怕；畏惧
n. 恐惧；畏惧
words.ex: He dreads going to the dentist.
words.ex_cn: 他害怕去看牙医。
words.en: If you dread something, you fear it intensely.

words.tr:
v. 耗尽；用完；使筋疲力尽
n. 排气管；废气
words.ex: The long hike exhausted him.
words.ex_cn: 这次漫长的徒步旅行让他筋疲力尽。
words.en: If something exhausts you, it makes you so tired, either physically or mentally, that you have no energy left.

words.ex: After running for an hour, he felt fatigue.
words.ex_cn: 跑了一个小时后，他感到疲乏。
words.en: A feeling of extreme physical or mental tiredness.

words.ex: He showed gratitude for the help.
words.ex_cn: 他表达了对帮助的感激。
words.en: Gratitude is the feeling of being thankful and appreciative.

words.ex: The hen is laying eggs in the coop.
words.ex_cn: 母鸡正在鸡舍里下蛋。
words.en: A hen is a female chicken, especially one that is kept for its eggs.

words.ex: He tries to memorize the words every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天试着记住这些单词。
words.en: To memorize something means to learn it so well that you can remember it perfectly.

words.ex: His neglect of the project caused delays.
words.ex_cn: 他对项目的疏忽导致了延误。
words.en: If you neglect someone or something, you fail to give them the attention or care that they need.

words.tr: adj. 挤满的；过度拥挤的；
words.ex: The bus was overcrowded at rush hour.
words.ex_cn: 高峰时段公交车挤满了人。
words.en: If a place is overcrowded, there are too many people or things in it.

words.ex: He possesses a small house near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 他拥有一栋靠近湖边的小房子。
words.en: If you possess something, you have it or own it.

words.ex: He sent the letter by postal service.
words.ex_cn: 他通过邮政服务寄了这封信。
words.en: Relating to the system for sending letters and parcels from one place to another.

words.tr: adj. 有希望的；有前途的； v. 承诺；答应；“promise”的现在分词；
words.ex: The young boy is a promising student.
words.ex_cn: 这个小男孩是个有希望的学生。
words.en: Showing signs of future success or achievement.

words.tr:
v. 牺牲；
n. 牺牲（品）；
words.ex: He sacrificed his time to help his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他牺牲了自己的时间来帮助朋友。
words.en: If you sacrifice something that is valuable or important, you give it up, usually to obtain something else for yourself or for other people.

words.ex: He solely depends on his bike to go to work.
words.ex_cn: 他只靠自行车去上班。
words.en: If something is solely the case, it is the only thing that is the case.

words.tr: adj. 令人吃惊的；出人意料的； v. “surprise”的现在分词；
words.ex: It was surprising that he passed the test.
words.ex_cn: 他通过了考试，这令人吃惊。
words.en: Causing surprise; unexpected.

words.ex: The unfamiliarity of the surroundings made her feel uneasy.
words.ex_cn: 对周围环境的陌生感让她感到不安。
words.en: The state of not being familiar with something or someone.

chapters.name: Unit 2 PASSAGE Ⅰ Phrases and Expressions

words.tr: 短语动词. 突然大哭起来；忍不住流下眼泪
words.ex: When she heard the sad news, she burst into tears.
words.ex_cn: 当她听到这个悲伤的消息时，她突然哭了起来。
words.en: To suddenly start crying.

words.tr: phrase. 阻止；抑制；使退缩；隐瞒
words.ex: He tried to hold back his tears.
words.ex_cn: 他试图忍住眼泪。
words.en: To hold back means to prevent someone or something from moving forward or making progress, or to keep something secret or not express your feelings.

words.tr: phrase. phr. 以不同的角度；用另一种眼光看待
words.ex: He saw his old friend in a different light after hearing his story.
words.ex_cn: 听完他的故事后，他以不同的眼光看待这位老朋友。
words.en: To consider or present something from a different perspective or in a new way.

chapters.name: Unit 2 PASSAGE Ⅱ New Words

words.tr:
n. 服务人员
adj. 随之而来的
words.ex: The attendant helped me find my seat.
words.ex_cn: 服务员帮我找到了座位。
words.en: An attendant is someone whose job is to serve or help people in a public place.

words.tr:
n. 屁股；乞丐；游民
v. 讨要；游荡
adj. 糟糕的；令人不快的
words.ex: He fell on his bum.
words.ex_cn: 他摔在了屁股上。
words.en: If someone is bumming around, they are spending time in a relaxed and lazy way, often without a fixed plan or purpose.

words.ex: The foreigner asked for directions to the train station.
words.ex_cn: 这位外国人问了去火车站的路。
words.en: A foreigner is a person who comes from a country other than your own.

words.tr:
v. 喘气；喘息；倒抽气
n. 喘气；喘息
words.ex: He gasped when he saw the big snake.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到那条大蛇时，他倒吸了一口冷气。
words.en: To take a short, quick breath through the mouth, especially because of surprise, pain, or shock.

words.ex: The car drove fast on the highway.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在高速公路上开得很快。
words.en: A highway is a main road, especially one that connects towns or cities.

words.tr: n. 厕所；洗手间；休息室；更衣室
words.ex: He went to the restroom after lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他午饭后去了洗手间。
words.en: A restroom is a room in a public building with toilets and sinks for people to use.

words.ex: The plane's takeoff was delayed by strong wind.
words.ex_cn: 飞机的起飞因强风而延误了。
words.en: Takeoff is the beginning of a flight, when an aircraft leaves the ground.

words.ex: He woke up with uncombed hair.
words.ex_cn: 他醒来时头发凌乱。
words.en: If someone's hair is uncombed, it is not neatly arranged and looks untidy.

words.ex: It is uncommon to see snow in this city.
words.ex_cn: 在这个城市看到雪是不常见的。
words.en: If you describe something as uncommon, you mean that it does not happen often or is not often seen.

chapters.name: Unit 2 PASSAGE Ⅱ Phrases and Expressions

words.ex: In the end, he chose to go home.
words.ex_cn: 最后，他选择回家。
words.en: finally, after everything has been considered or done

words.ex: He is the best player in the world.
words.ex_cn: 他是世界上最好的球员。
words.en: Used to emphasize the question of what exists or happens in the world, or to emphasize a superlative.

words.tr: phrase. （把车）靠边停下；靠边停车
words.ex: The police told him to pull over.
words.ex_cn: 警察让他靠边停车。
words.en: To move a vehicle to the side of the road and stop, especially when instructed by the police.

words.tr: phrase. 出现；生产；结果是；关闭；朝外
words.ex: The weather turned out to be sunny.
words.ex_cn: 天气结果是晴朗的。
words.en: If something turns out a particular way, it happens in that way or has the result or degree of success indicated. If you turn out something, you produce or create it. If you turn out a light, you switch it off.

chapters.name: Unit 3 Part Two New Words

words.ex: He felt proud of his academic achievement.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的学业成就感到自豪。
words.en: An achievement is something which someone has succeeded in doing, especially after a lot of effort.

words.ex: He dressed appropriately for the interview.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着得体地去参加了面试。
words.en: In a way that is suitable or proper in the circumstances.

words.ex: He showed great capability in solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他在解决数学问题上展现了很强的能力。
words.en: The ability or qualities necessary to do something.

words.ex: He has the capacity to solve hard math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他有能力解决复杂的数学问题。
words.en: The capacity of a place or container is the amount of things or people that it can hold.

words.tr: v. 贡献；促成；捐献；投稿；
words.ex: He contributes money to the charity.
words.ex_cn: 他向慈善机构捐款。
words.en: If you contribute to something, you help to cause it or make it happen.

words.tr: adv. 创造性地；有创造力地；
words.ex: She painted creatively using only her fingers.
words.ex_cn: 她用手指创造性地绘画。
words.en: In a way that involves the use of imagination or original ideas to create something.

words.ex: The cruelty of the bully made the child cry.
words.ex_cn: 这个欺凌者的残忍让那个孩子哭了。
words.en: Cruelty is behaviour that deliberately causes pain or distress to people or animals.

words.ex: Children show dependence on their parents.
words.ex_cn: 孩子对父母有依赖。
words.en: The state of relying on or being controlled by someone or something else.

words.ex: He dominates the conversation.
words.ex_cn: 他主宰了谈话。
words.en: To dominate means to control or govern someone or something, or to be the most important or noticeable feature of something.

words.ex: The shopkeeper will evaluate the old watch.
words.ex_cn: 店主将估价这块旧手表。
words.en: If you evaluate something or someone, you consider them in order to make a judgment about them, for example about how good or bad they are.

words.ex: She is flexible with her schedule.
words.ex_cn: 她的日程安排很灵活。
words.en: Able to change or be changed easily according to the situation.

words.tr: adv. 由衷地；真诚地；真正地；
words.ex: I genuinely appreciate your help.
words.ex_cn: 我由衷地感谢你的帮助。
words.en: If you describe something as genuine, you mean that it is real and exactly what it appears to be.

words.ex: His genuineness made everyone trust him.
words.ex_cn: 他的真诚让所有人都信任他。
words.en: The quality of being genuine; authenticity.

words.ex: He felt guilt after lying to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他在对朋友撒谎后感到内疚。
words.en: Guilt is an unhappy feeling that you have because you have done something wrong or think that you have done something wrong.

words.ex: The child felt helpless when he lost his mother.
words.ex_cn: 当孩子失去妈妈时，他感到无助。
words.en: Unable to defend oneself or to act without help.

words.ex: The food supply was inadequate for the number of people.
words.ex_cn: 食物供应对人数来说是不充分的。
words.en: If something is inadequate, there is not enough of it or it is not good enough.

words.ex: The country gained independence in 1960.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家在1960年获得了独立。
words.en: Independence is the freedom from control or influence of others, allowing one to make decisions and act on one's own.

words.ex: He lives independently and makes his own decisions.
words.ex_cn: 他独立生活，并自己做决定。
words.en: If one thing or person is independent of another, they are separate and not connected, so that the first one is not affected or influenced by the second.

words.ex: The limitation of the phone is its short battery life.
words.ex_cn: 这款手机的限制是电池续航时间短。
words.en: A limitation is a rule or situation that restricts what you can do or what can happen.

words.ex: He didn't give up, even though some called him a loser.
words.ex_cn: 他没有放弃，即使有些人称他为失败者。
words.en: A loser is someone who is not successful in a particular situation or who does not achieve what they set out to do.

words.ex: He tried to manipulate the results to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 他试图操纵结果来赢得比赛。
words.en: To manipulate something means to handle or control it skillfully, often in a way that is considered unfair or dishonest.

words.ex: Eating vegetables gives you good nutrition.
words.ex_cn: 吃蔬菜能提供良好的营养。
words.en: The process of providing or obtaining the food necessary for health and growth.

words.tr:
n. 潜力；
adj. 潜在的；
words.ex: The young athlete shows great potential.
words.ex_cn: 这位年轻运动员展现出巨大的潜力。
words.en: If you say that someone or something has potential, you mean that they have the necessary abilities or qualities to become successful or useful in the future.

words.tr:
n. 一系列；（变化）范围；山脉；
v. （在某范围内）变化；包括（各种不同的人或物）；
words.ex: The store offers a range of colors.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店提供一系列颜色。
words.en: A range of things is a number of different things of the same general kind.

words.tr: adj. 易反应的；应答的；回答的；
words.ex: The child is responsive to his mother's voice.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子对母亲的声音反应灵敏。
words.en: If someone or something is responsive, they react quickly and favorably.

words.tr: adj. 刻板的；坚硬的；严格的；
words.ex: He has a rigid attitude toward rules.
words.ex_cn: 他对规则的态度很刻板。
words.en: not able to be changed or adapted; not able to be bent or moved; stiff

words.ex: He is a trustworthy friend who always keeps his promises.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个值得信赖的朋友，总是信守承诺。
words.en: If you describe someone as trustworthy, you mean they are reliable, honest, and truthful.

words.tr: adj. 没意识到的；不知道的；
words.ex: He was unaware of the rain until he got wet.
words.ex_cn: 他直到被淋湿了才意识到下雨了。
words.en: If you are unaware of something, you do not know about it.

words.ex: This painting is unique because no other like it exists.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画是独特的，因为没有其他类似的。
words.en: Something that is unique is the only one of its kind.

words.ex: The uniqueness of her voice made her famous.
words.ex_cn: 她声音的唯一性让她成名。
words.en: The quality of being the only one of its kind.

chapters.name: Unit 3 Part Two Phrases and Expressions

words.tr: phrase. 呼吁；号召；要求；接（人）
words.ex: The situation calls for immediate action.
words.ex_cn: 这种情况需要立即采取行动。
words.en: If you call for something, you demand that it should happen.

words.tr:
n. 海峡；渠道；河床；频道；
v. 引导；
words.ex: The English Channel separates England from France.
words.ex_cn: 英吉利海峡将英格兰与法国分隔开。
words.en: A channel is a television station and the programs that it broadcasts. A channel is also a method or system that people use to send information, goods, etc. to each other.

words.tr: phrase. 贡献；促成；导致；有助于
words.ex: Volunteers contribute to the clean-up of the park.
words.ex_cn: 志愿者们为公园的清洁做出了贡献。
words.en: If you contribute to something, you help to cause it or make it happen.

words.tr: phrase. 进入；包括；参与；成为...一部分
words.ex: He will enter into the room after knocking.
words.ex_cn: 他敲门后会进入房间。
words.en: To begin or become involved in an activity, agreement, or condition.

words.tr: phrase. 凭自身的能力或资格；独立地；本身
words.ex: She is a successful artist in her own right.
words.ex_cn: 她本身就是一个成功的艺术家。
words.en: If someone is a particular kind of person in their own right, they are that kind of person because of their own efforts, talents, or qualities, and not because of their connection with someone else.

words.ex: He stayed calm in the face of danger.
words.ex_cn: 他在危险面前保持冷静。
words.en: If you do something in the face of a particular situation, you do it despite the difficulties or problems that the situation causes.

words.tr: phrase. 不辜负；做到；实践（诺言等）
words.ex: He tried hard to live up to his father's expectations.
words.ex_cn: 他努力不辜负父亲的期望。
words.en: To perform as well as or achieve what is expected or promised.

words.ex: People often refer to the city as the 'Big Apple'.
words.ex_cn: 人们常把这座城市称作“大苹果”。
words.en: To call someone or something by a particular name or title.

words.ex: Many people see pollution as a big problem.
words.ex_cn: 许多人认为污染是一个大问题。
words.en: To consider or regard someone or something in a particular way.

chapters.name: Unit 3 PASSAGE Ⅰ New Words

words.tr: n. 锻造；打铁；“blacksmith”的现在分词
words.ex: He practices blacksmithing in his small workshop.
words.ex_cn: 他在自己的小作坊里练习打铁。
words.en: Blacksmithing is the craft of forging iron into useful or ornamental objects.

words.tr: n. 蓝知更鸟（产于北美）
words.ex: A bluebird sits on the tree branch.
words.ex_cn: 一只蓝鸟停在树枝上。
words.en: A bluebird is a small North American songbird with a blue back and wings and a reddish breast.

words.tr:
n. 旁路；
v. 绕过；
words.ex: The city built a bypass around the old town.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市建了一条绕过老城区的旁路。
words.en: If you bypass a place or a system, you avoid it or go around it instead of going through it.

words.tr: adj. 铁石心肠的；无情的；起老茧的
words.ex: He was callous to his friend's pain.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友的痛苦无动于衷。
words.en: A callous person or action is very cruel and shows no concern for other people or their feelings.

words.ex: He felt deep depression after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到深深的抑郁。
words.en: A period during which business, employment, and stock-market values decline severely or remain at a very low level of activity.

words.ex: He signed up for enlistment last month.
words.ex_cn: 他上个月报名参军了。
words.en: The act of joining the armed forces voluntarily or the process of being recruited into the armed forces.

words.ex: The teacher showed fairness in grading all students.
words.ex_cn: 老师在给所有学生评分时展现了公平。
words.en: Fairness is the quality of treating people equally or in a way that is right or reasonable.

words.ex: The ferryboat takes people across the river every hour.
words.ex_cn: 渡船每小时运送人们过河。
words.en: A ferryboat is a boat that transports passengers and sometimes also vehicles, usually across a river or a short stretch of sea.

words.ex: The fireman saved the cat from the tree.
words.ex_cn: 消防员从树上救下了那只猫。
words.en: A fireman is a person whose job is to put out fires and rescue people from dangerous situations, especially in buildings.

words.tr: adj. 天真无邪的；无辜的；
words.ex: The innocent child smiled at the stranger.
words.ex_cn: 那个天真无邪的孩子对陌生人笑了。
words.en: If someone is innocent, they did not commit a crime which they have been accused of.

words.ex: He bought insurance for his car.
words.ex_cn: 他为他的车买了保险。
words.en: Insurance is an arrangement in which you pay money to a company, and they pay money to you if something unpleasant happens to you, for example if your property is stolen or damaged, or if you get a serious illness.

words.tr:
v. 绑架；劫持；诱拐
n. 绑架罪
words.ex: The man tried to kidnap the little girl.
words.ex_cn: 这个人试图绑架那个小女孩。
words.en: To take someone away illegally by force, typically to obtain a ransom.

words.ex: The kidnapper took the boy and demanded money.
words.ex_cn: 绑匪绑架了那个男孩并索要赎金。
words.en: A kidnapper is a person who abducts someone and holds them captive, typically to demand a ransom.

words.ex: The locomotive pulled the train down the track.
words.ex_cn: 机车拉着火车沿着轨道行驶。
words.en: A locomotive is a powered rail vehicle used for pulling trains.

words.ex: He felt miserable after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到很悲惨。
words.en: If you are miserable, you are very unhappy.

words.tr: adj. 奇怪的；奇数的；余的；
words.ex: He wore an odd hat to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一顶奇怪的帽子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as odd, you mean that they are strange or unusual.

words.tr: n. 养老金；退休金；抚恤金；
words.ex: He receives a monthly pension after retiring.
words.ex_cn: 他退休后每月领取养老金。
words.en: A pension is a sum of money which a retired, widowed, or disabled person regularly receives from the state or from a former employer.

words.tr: n. 游戏时间，娱乐时间
words.ex: The children are having playtime in the park.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们正在公园里玩耍。
words.en: The time allowed for children to play.

words.ex: She is pregnant and will have a baby next month.
words.ex_cn: 她怀孕了，下个月就要生宝宝了。
words.en: Having a baby developing in the uterus.

words.ex: He worked hard and prospered in business.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作，在商业上取得了成功。
words.en: If people or businesses prosper, they are successful and do well.

words.tr: adj. 不同寻常的；非凡的；显著的；值得注意的；
words.ex: She made a remarkable improvement in just one month.
words.ex_cn: 她在短短一个月内取得了不同寻常的进步。
words.en: Unusual or striking in a way that attracts attention.

words.ex: He resents being ignored by his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他怨恨被老板忽视。
words.en: If you resent someone or something, you feel bitter and angry about them.

words.ex: He tried to resist the temptation to eat sweets.
words.ex_cn: 他试图抵制吃甜食的诱惑。
words.en: If you resist something such as a change, you refuse to accept it and try to prevent it.

words.ex: He will retire next year.
words.ex_cn: 他明年将退休。
words.en: If you retire, you stop working, usually because you have reached a certain age or because you are ill.

words.tr: adj. 失控的；物价飞涨的；
words.ex: The runaway train crashed into the station.
words.ex_cn: 这列失控的火车撞上了车站。
words.en: A runaway is someone who has run away from home or an institution, or something that is out of control and moving or acting without being directed.

words.tr:
n. 时距；跨度；
v. 跨越；
words.ex: The span of his career was 40 years.
words.ex_cn: 他职业生涯的时距是40年。
words.en: The extent or measure of space between two points or extremities, as of a bridge or a roof; the full extent, stretch, or reach of anything.

words.ex: The succession of rain made the ground wet.
words.ex_cn: 连续的雨水使地面变湿了。
words.en: A succession of things of the same kind is a number of them that exist or happen one after the other.

words.tr: n. 黄昏；薄暮；暮光；衰退期
words.ex: The birds fly home at twilight.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿在黄昏时飞回家。
words.en: The time of day immediately following sunset, or the period of time at the end of the day when the sun is just below the horizon, especially the period between sunset and dark.

words.tr: adj. 未破的；不间断的；未驯服的（马）
words.ex: The unbroken chain of events led to the accident.
words.ex_cn: 这一连串未被打断的事件导致了事故。
words.en: If something is unbroken, it is continuous or complete and has not been interrupted or damaged.

words.ex: She put the clothes in the washer.
words.ex_cn: 她把衣服放进洗衣机里。
words.en: A washer is a machine that washes clothes, or a person whose job is to wash clothes, or a flat ring made of metal, rubber, or plastic that is used to make a joint tight.

chapters.name: Unit 3 PASSAGE Ⅰ Phrases and Expressions

words.tr: phrase. 继续；坚持；进行；开展
words.ex: He will carry on working after lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他午饭后会继续工作。
words.en: If you carry on, you continue doing something.

words.ex: He decided to drop out of the competition.
words.ex_cn: 他决定不参加比赛。
words.en: If someone drops out of a school or a course, they leave it before they have finished it.

words.ex: He decided to drop out of the game because he was tired.
words.ex_cn: 他因为累了决定不参与比赛。
words.en: To leave a school, college, or course of study before you have finished it.

words.tr: phrase. 赠送；分发；背叛；泄露
words.ex: He will give away his old books to the library.
words.ex_cn: 他将把他的旧书捐给图书馆。
words.en: To give something to someone without asking for payment, or to reveal something secret or private.

words.tr: 短语动词. 出发；上路；开始旅行
words.ex: He hit the road early to avoid traffic.
words.ex_cn: 他早早上路以避开交通拥堵。
words.en: To begin a journey or to leave a place to go somewhere else.

words.tr: phrase. 用完；耗尽；跑出去；到期
words.ex: We run out of milk every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 我们每星期天都把牛奶喝光了。
words.en: If you run out of something, you have no more of it left.

chapters.name: Unit 3 PASSAGE Ⅱ New Words

words.ex: He finally acknowledged his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他终于承认了自己的错误。
words.en: If you acknowledge a fact or a situation, you accept or admit that it is true or that it exists.

words.tr:
adj. 简短的；简明的；短暂的；
v. 为…提供信息；
n. 摘要；概要；
words.ex: He gave a brief answer.
words.ex_cn: 他给出了一个简短的答案。
words.en: If something is brief, it lasts only for a short time.

words.ex: Under these circumstances, we had to cancel the trip.
words.ex_cn: 在这种情况下，我们不得不取消旅行。
words.en: A circumstance is a fact or event that makes a situation the way it is.

words.tr: n. 代表大会；议会；国会；
words.ex: The congress met to discuss new laws.
words.ex_cn: 代表大会召开以讨论新法律。
words.en: A congress is a formal meeting of representatives, as of various nations, to discuss problems or to make decisions.

words.tr:
v. 选择；挑选；
adj. 精心挑选的；
words.ex: He will select the best candidate for the job.
words.ex_cn: 他将选择最适合这份工作的人。
words.en: If you select something, you choose it from a number of things of the same kind.

words.ex: He decided to embark on a new career.
words.ex_cn: 他决定从事一份新职业。
words.en: To embark on something means to start it, especially something new, difficult, or exciting.

words.ex: The empire ruled many countries long ago.
words.ex_cn: 这个帝国很久以前统治了许多国家。
words.en: An empire is a group of countries or territories that are under the control of a single ruler or government.

words.ex: He showed excellence in math competitions.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学竞赛中表现出色。
words.en: The quality of being outstanding or extremely good.

words.ex: The body expels waste through the kidneys.
words.ex_cn: 身体通过肾脏排出废物。
words.en: If someone is expelled from a school or organization, they are officially told to leave because they have behaved badly or broken the rules.

words.ex: The children were exposed to cold weather without coats.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在没有外套的情况下遭受了寒冷天气。
words.en: To expose something means to uncover it so that it can be seen, or to make it known or public.

words.tr: adj. 联邦的；联邦制的；联邦政府的；
words.ex: The federal government passed a new law.
words.ex_cn: 联邦政府通过了一项新法律。
words.en: A federal system of government is one in which there is a central government and separate governments for each of the states or regions.

words.ex: He is a former teacher who now works as a writer.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名以前的老师，现在是一名作家。
words.en: Former is used to describe someone who used to have a particular job, position, or role, but no longer has it.

words.tr: adj. 光辉的； v. “glow”的现在分词；
words.ex: The glowing sun rose over the hills.
words.ex_cn: 光辉的太阳从山上升起。
words.en: If you describe something as glowing, you mean that it is very positive and enthusiastic.

words.tr: adj. 卑微的；谦逊的；虚心的；
words.ex: He lived in a humble house near the river.
words.ex_cn: 他住在河边一座简陋的房子里。
words.en: If you describe someone as humble, you mean that they do not think they are better or more important than other people.

words.tr: adj. 偏远的；隔离的；孤独的； v. 使隔离；“isolate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The village is isolated, far from any city.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄很偏远，远离任何城市。
words.en: If something is isolated, it is far away from other places, buildings, or people.

words.tr: n. 领导才能；领导地位；
words.ex: His leadership helped the team win the match.
words.ex_cn: 他的领导才能帮助团队赢得了比赛。
words.en: Leadership is the ability to lead, guide, or direct a group, organization, or country.

words.tr: adj. 很长的；漫长的；冗长的；
words.ex: The meeting was lengthy and tiring.
words.ex_cn: 会议很长，很累人。
words.en: Something that is lengthy lasts for a long time, often longer than you want or expect.

words.tr: n. 勋爵；主；上帝；统治者；
words.ex: The lord lived in a big castle.
words.ex_cn: 这位勋爵住在一座大城堡里。
words.en: A lord is a man who has a high rank in the nobility, especially in Britain, or a man who has authority or control over others.

words.tr:
adj. 军事的；军用的；
n. 军队；武装力量；
words.ex: The military base is near the border.
words.ex_cn: 军事基地靠近边境。
words.en: relating to or characteristic of soldiers or armed forces

words.ex: He got a nomination for best actor.
words.ex_cn: 他获得了最佳男演员的提名。
words.en: The act of officially suggesting someone or something for a position, prize, or honor.

words.tr: adj. 首要的；主要的；基本的；最好的；
words.ex: This is the prime reason for the delay.
words.ex_cn: 这是延误的首要原因。
words.en: Prime is used to describe something that is of the best possible quality, or the most important or basic part of something.

words.ex: His pursuit of happiness made him work hard every day.
words.ex_cn: 他对幸福的追求让他每天努力工作。
words.en: The act of pursuing something or someone, especially in order to catch or achieve them.

words.ex: He reject the job offer.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝了这份工作邀请。
words.en: If you reject something such as a proposal, a request, or an offer, you do not accept it or you do not agree to it.

words.ex: He faces renomination for the same position next year.
words.ex_cn: 他明年将面临同一职位的再次提名。
words.en: The act of nominating someone again for a position or award.

words.ex: The senate voted to pass the new law.
words.ex_cn: 参议院投票通过了这项新法律。
words.en: The Senate is the smaller and more important of the two parts of the parliament in some countries, for example in the United States and Australia.

words.ex: The statesman spoke wisely to calm the nation.
words.ex_cn: 这位政治家明智地讲话以安抚国家。
words.en: A statesman is a respected political leader or figure, especially one who has had a long and successful career in politics.

words.tr: adj. 没有希望的；无前途的；不乐观的
words.ex: The weather looks unpromising for a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 天气看起来不适合野餐。
words.en: If you describe something as unpromising, you think that it is unlikely to be successful or produce anything good in the future.

words.tr: n. 代理；副职；恶习；缺点；
words.ex: He acted as vice for the manager during her absence.
words.ex_cn: 在经理缺席期间，他担任代理。
words.en: A vice is a moral fault or weakness in someone's character.

chapters.name: Unit 3 PASSAGE Ⅱ Phrases and Expressions

words.ex: He gave up smoking last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年戒烟了。
words.en: If you give up something, you stop doing it or having it.

words.tr: phrase. 在国内和国外；海内外
words.ex: He works at home and abroad.
words.ex_cn: 他在国内和国外工作。
words.en: Both within one's own country and in foreign countries.

words.tr: phrase. 在国内和国外；海内外
words.ex: The company sells products at home and abroad.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司在国内和国外都销售产品。
words.en: both domestically and internationally

chapters.name: Unit 4 Part Two New Words

words.tr: n. 流血；失血； v. “bleed”的现在分词；
words.ex: The cut caused heavy bleeding.
words.ex_cn: 伤口导致大量流血。
words.en: The process of losing blood from the body as a result of injury or illness.

words.ex: He took a capsule for his headache.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了一粒胶囊来缓解头痛。
words.en: A capsule is a small container or case, especially one that is sealed and contains a dose of medicine, or a spacecraft's compartment for astronauts.

words.ex: The small spider is harmless.
words.ex_cn: 这只小蜘蛛是无害的。
words.en: If someone or something is harmless, they are not dangerous and do not cause any harm.

words.ex: The wound will heal in a few days.
words.ex_cn: 伤口几天后就会愈合。
words.en: To make or become healthy or whole again; to cure or recover from an injury or illness.

words.ex: The doctor gave him a placebo to see if his pain would go away.
words.ex_cn: 医生给了他一个安慰剂，看看他的疼痛是否会消失。
words.en: A substance that has no therapeutic effect, used as a control in testing new drugs, or given for its psychological effect to a patient who believes it to be a medicine.

words.ex: The doctor prescribed medicine for my cold.
words.ex_cn: 医生给我开了治疗感冒的药。
words.en: If a doctor prescribes medicine or treatment for you, he or she tells you what medicine or treatment to have.

words.ex: The doctor wrote a prescription for medicine.
words.ex_cn: 医生开了一张药方。
words.en: A prescription is a written order from a physician for the preparation and administration of a drug or device for a patient.

words.ex: His reaction was quick when the ball came at him.
words.ex_cn: 当球朝他飞来时，他的反应很快。
words.en: Your reaction to something that has happened or something that you have experienced is what you feel, say, or do because of it.

words.ex: The movie shows a fantasy, not reality.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影展示的是幻想，而不是现实。
words.en: Reality is the state of things as they actually exist, rather than as they may appear or might be imagined.

words.ex: His smile gave me reassurance.
words.ex_cn: 他的微笑让我安心。
words.en: If someone needs reassurance, they are very worried and need someone to help them stop worrying by saying kind or helpful things.

words.ex: He felt seasickness on the boat.
words.ex_cn: 他在船上感到晕船。
words.en: Nausea and dizziness caused by the motion of a ship at sea.

words.ex: He swore he didn't steal the money.
words.ex_cn: 他发誓他没有偷钱。
words.en: If someone swears, they use language that is considered to be rude or offensive, usually because they are angry.

words.ex: The doctor gave him proper treatment for the infection.
words.ex_cn: 医生给他提供了针对感染的适当治疗。
words.en: The act or manner of treating someone or something, especially in a medical context.

words.ex: The tribal people live in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 部落的人住在森林里。
words.en: Tribal relates to a tribe or tribes.

words.ex: He has an ulcer from eating too much spicy food.
words.ex_cn: 他因为吃太多辣食而得了溃疡。
words.en: An ulcer is a sore area on the skin or inside the body that is very painful and may bleed or produce a poisonous substance.

chapters.name: Unit 4 Part Two Phrases and Expressions

words.ex: He didn't study hard, as a result, he failed the test.
words.ex_cn: 他没有努力学习，结果考试不及格。
words.en: used to introduce the consequence or effect of a particular situation or event

words.ex: He fooled his friend into eating a spicy pepper.
words.ex_cn: 他骗他的朋友吃了一个辣椒。
words.en: To deceive someone into doing something.

words.ex: In a way, he is right about the problem.
words.ex_cn: 在某种程度上，他对这个问题的看法是正确的。
words.en: To some extent; from a certain point of view.

words.tr: phrase. 畅所欲言；打开；开放
words.ex: Please open up and tell me how you really feel.
words.ex_cn: 请畅所欲言，告诉我你真正的感受。
words.en: To make something available or accessible; to start or begin something.

words.ex: The decision rests with you.
words.ex_cn: 决定权在你。
words.en: To be the responsibility or decision of a particular person or group.

chapters.name: Unit 4 PASSAGE Ⅰ New Words

words.tr:
n. 账户；叙述；账目；
v. 占…；说明；
words.ex: I opened a bank account last week.
words.ex_cn: 我上周开了一家银行账户。
words.en: An account is a detailed report or description of an event or situation.

words.tr: adj. 上瘾了的；入了迷的
words.ex: He is addicted to video games.
words.ex_cn: 他沉迷于电子游戏。
words.en: If you are addicted to something, you cannot stop doing it or using it, even though it may be harmful to you.

words.ex: He has an addiction to video games.
words.ex_cn: 他对电子游戏上瘾了。
words.en: Addiction is the condition of being unable to stop using or doing something as a habit, especially something harmful.

words.ex: The company will advertise its new phone on TV.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司将在电视上为新手机登广告。
words.en: If you advertise something such as a product, an event, or a job, you tell people about it in newspapers, on television, or on posters in order to encourage them to buy the product, go to the event, or apply for the job.

words.ex: The advertiser showed a new TV commercial.
words.ex_cn: 广告商播放了一则新的电视广告。
words.en: An advertiser is a person or company that pays for a product, service, or event to be advertised.

words.tr:
n. 预算；预算金额；
adj. 廉价的；花钱少的；
v. 为 ... 做预算；
words.ex: We made a budget for our vacation.
words.ex_cn: 我们为旅行制定了一个预算。
words.en: A budget is a plan that shows how much money a person or organization will earn and how much they will need or be able to spend.

words.tr: n. 强迫；强制；难以抗拒的冲动
words.ex: He felt a compulsion to check the door again.
words.ex_cn: 他感到一种必须再次检查门的强迫感。
words.en: A compulsion is a very strong desire to do something, which you find difficult to control.

words.tr: adj. 无法控制行为的；禁不住的；
words.ex: He has a compulsive habit of checking the door lock.
words.ex_cn: 他有一种无法控制地检查门锁的习惯。
words.en: If you describe someone or their behaviour as compulsive, you mean that they cannot stop themselves doing or wanting something, even though it may be harmful or unreasonable.

words.tr:
n. 信用；赊账；赞扬；贷款；荣誉；
v. 相信；
words.ex: He has good credit with the bank.
words.ex_cn: 他在银行有良好的信用。
words.en: If you are allowed credit, you are allowed to pay for goods or services several weeks or months after you have received them.

words.tr:
n. 折扣；
v. 不全信；不重视；
words.ex: The store gave a 20% discount on all shoes.
words.ex_cn: 商店对所有鞋子提供了20%的折扣。
words.en: A reduction in the usual price of something, or the act of reducing the price.

words.ex: The hunter caught a deer in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 猎人在森林里捕到了一只鹿。
words.en: A hunter is a person who hunts wild animals for food or as a sport.

words.tr:
n. 影响（力）；
v. 影响；
words.ex: The teacher had a big influence on her students.
words.ex_cn: 老师对学生们有很大的影响。
words.en: The power to affect, control, or manipulate someone or something.

words.ex: His refusal to listen is irrational.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝倾听是不合理的。
words.en: If you describe someone's feelings and behavior as irrational, you mean they are not based on logical reasons or clear thinking.

words.ex: His personality is very friendly and outgoing.
words.ex_cn: 他的个性非常友好和外向。
words.en: The combination of characteristics or qualities that form an individual's distinctive character.

words.ex: He felt psychological stress before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试前感到心理压力。
words.en: Relating to the mental and emotional state of a person.

words.ex: The book is reasonably expensive.
words.ex_cn: 这本书相当地贵。
words.en: In a fair and sensible way; to a moderate or acceptable degree.

words.tr: v. 反映；反射；反省；思考；仔细考虑；
words.ex: The mirror reflects the sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 镜子反射阳光。
words.en: If a surface reflects light, heat, sound, or an image, it sends the light, etc. back and does not absorb it. If something is reflected in a mirror or in water, you can see its image in the mirror or in the water.

words.ex: The salesclerk helped the customer find the right size.
words.ex_cn: 售货员帮助顾客找到了合适的尺码。
words.en: A salesclerk is a person whose job is to serve customers in a store.

words.ex: He shows self-discipline by waking up early every day.
words.ex_cn: 他通过每天早起展现自律。
words.en: The ability to control yourself and to make yourself work hard or behave in a particular way without needing anyone else to tell you what to do.

words.tr:
n. 茎；词干；
v. 起源于(~ from)；
words.ex: The flower grows on a long green stem.
words.ex_cn: 花长在一根长长的绿色茎上。
words.en: The main body or stalk of a plant or shrub, typically rising above ground but occasionally subterranean; to stop or restrict (the flow of something).

words.ex: The dove is a symbol of peace.
words.ex_cn: 鸽子是和平的象征。
words.en: A symbol is a shape or design that is used to represent something such as an idea, a quality, or a process.

words.ex: The therapist helped him feel better after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 治疗专家在事故后帮助他感觉好些了。
words.en: A therapist is a person who is skilled in a particular type of therapy and treats people using it.

chapters.name: Unit 4 PASSAGE Ⅰ Phrases and Expressions

words.ex: I like fruits, for instance, apples and bananas.
words.ex_cn: 我喜欢水果，例如苹果和香蕉。
words.en: Used to introduce an example that illustrates or supports a point being made.

words.tr: phrase. v. 紧紧抓住某物；坚持保留某物
words.ex: Please hold on to your bag in the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 在人群中请抓好你的包。
words.en: To keep something in one's possession; to not let go of something.

words.ex: He likes apples. In addition, he likes oranges.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢苹果。另外，他喜欢橙子。
words.en: You use in addition when you want to mention another item connected with the subject you are discussing.

words.tr: phrase. 赊账；以赊购方式；信用交易
words.ex: He bought the bike on credit.
words.ex_cn: 他用赊账的方式买了这辆自行车。
words.en: If you buy something on credit, you pay for it at a later time, usually paying interest as well as the original cost.

words.ex: His love of music stems from his childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他对音乐的热爱源于他的童年。
words.en: If a condition or problem stems from something, it was caused originally by that thing.

chapters.name: Unit 4 PASSAGE Ⅱ New Words

words.ex: He analyzes data every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天分析数据。
words.en: To examine something methodically and in detail, typically in order to explain and interpret it.

words.ex: The loud noise was an annoyance to everyone.
words.ex_cn: 那阵噪音让每个人都感到烦恼。
words.en: Annoyance is the feeling of being slightly angry or impatient.

words.tr: n. 权威；官方机构；权力；权威人士；当局；
words.ex: The teacher is an authority on ancient history.
words.ex_cn: 这位老师是古代史方面的权威。
words.en: The power to make decisions or enforce rules.

words.tr: adj. 自动化的； v. “automate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The factory uses automated machines to make cars.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂使用自动化机器来制造汽车。
words.en: An automated machine or process is one that operates by itself without needing human control.

words.ex: He cited a book in his essay.
words.ex_cn: 他在文章中引用了一本书。
words.en: To cite something means to quote it or mention it as evidence or proof of what you are saying.

words.tr:
adj. 计算机化的；有关计算机的
v. 使计算机化；用计算机做；“computerize”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The school uses computerized tests for math.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校使用计算机化考试来测数学。
words.en: If something is computerized, it is done or controlled by computers.

words.tr:
adj. 动态的；有活力的；不断变化的；
n. 活力；动力；
words.ex: The game has dynamic weather that changes every hour.
words.ex_cn: 这个游戏有每小时变化的动态天气。
words.en: If you describe someone as dynamic, you approve of them because they are full of energy or full of new ideas.

words.ex: He fixed the electrical wire with tape.
words.ex_cn: 他用胶带修好了电线。
words.en: Relating to electricity or things that use electricity.

words.ex: They will extend the deadline by one week.
words.ex_cn: 他们将截止日期延长一周。
words.en: To extend something means to make it longer or larger, or to spread it over a larger area.

words.ex: The foundation gives money to poor students.
words.ex_cn: 这个基金会向贫困学生提供资金。
words.en: The foundation of something such as a belief or way of life is the things on which it is based.

words.ex: He shouted with fury when he lost the game.
words.ex_cn: 当他输掉比赛时，他愤怒地大喊。
words.en: Fury is a feeling of intense anger.

words.ex: The judge made a fair decision to show justice.
words.ex_cn: 法官做出了公正的裁决以体现公正。
words.en: Justice is fairness in the way that people are treated.

words.ex: She will lengthen the dress for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她会把裙子改长一点去参加派对。
words.en: To make something longer, or to become longer.

words.tr: v. 减到最少；使最小化；
words.ex: Try to minimize waste in the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 尽量减少厨房里的浪费。
words.en: To minimize something means to reduce it to the smallest possible amount or degree.

words.ex: The neighbouring town has a big market.
words.ex_cn: 邻近的城镇有一个大市场。
words.en: Neighbouring places are next to or near each other.

words.tr: n. 观察；观测；注意；监视；(观察后的）意见；
words.ex: The scientist made an observation about the bird's behavior.
words.ex_cn: 科学家对这只鸟的行为进行了观察。
words.en: The act of noticing or watching something carefully in order to gain information.

words.tr: adj. 较合意的；更可取的；
words.ex: Tea is preferable to coffee in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 早上喝茶比喝咖啡更合意。
words.en: If you say that one thing is preferable to another, you mean that it is more desirable or suitable.

words.tr:
n. 长队；
v. 排队；
words.ex: There is a long queue at the ticket counter.
words.ex_cn: 售票处排着一条长队。
words.en: A queue is a line of people or vehicles waiting for something.

words.tr: v. 要求归还；收回；开垦；感化
words.ex: He wants to reclaim his lost wallet.
words.ex_cn: 他想要要求归还他丢失的钱包。
words.en: If you reclaim something that you have lost or that has been taken away from you, you succeed in getting it back. If you reclaim land, you make it suitable for use, for example by draining it or by getting rid of unwanted buildings or plants.

words.tr: n. 讲述者；（银行）出纳员；
words.ex: The old man is the teller of fairy tales.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人是童话故事的讲述者。
words.en: A teller is a person who works in a bank and whose job includes receiving and paying out money.

words.ex: The train stops at the terminus.
words.ex_cn: 火车在终点站停下。
words.en: A terminus is the end of a transportation line or the station at the end of a railway or bus route.

words.tr:
v. 转移；转让；调任；
n. 转移；转让；调任；
words.ex: He will transfer the money to his bank account.
words.ex_cn: 他将把钱转到他的银行账户。
